# Reliability Requirements Checklist: Candidate Route Baseline and Role Contracts

**Purpose**: Assess whether evidence freshness, source applicability and invalidation, deterministic artifact agreement, fixture and telemetry handoff, classified unknowns, and the one-working-day terminal decision are complete, clear, consistent, and reviewable.
**Created**: 2026-07-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Evidence Freshness and Authority

- [x] CHK001 Are official OpenAI sources the exclusive authority for platform facts and pinned tracked repository files the authority for project facts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016–FR-017]
- [x] CHK002 Does every platform fact require an exact locator, retrieval date, target surface, feature, documented scope, applicability, conflict state, and invalidation trigger? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017; Data Model §ProvenanceRecord]
- [x] CHK003 Is freshness objectively bounded so official and environment evidence supporting `go` is retrieved or observed during the recorded workday while project evidence matches the pinned research revision? [Measurability, Spec §FR-017; Contract §Evidence and surfaces]
- [x] CHK004 Are historical or version claims kept within their documented scope instead of treating release-note recency as proof of current cross-surface behavior? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications Session 1 and §FR-016]
- [x] CHK005 Are unavailable, stale, or unverifiable sources prevented from supporting a fact or passing completion check until revalidated or reclassified? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §FR-017–FR-019; Data Model §ProvenanceRecord]
- [x] CHK006 Are tracked, cached, and installed observations separated so local freshness cannot override the tracked production contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005; Data Model §SourceObservation]

## Applicability, Conflict, and Invalidation

- [x] CHK007 Are `cli`, `desktop_app`, `app_server`, and `non_interactive` represented independently, with no evidence inheritance between surfaces? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020; Data Model §SurfaceRecord]
- [x] CHK008 Are source silence and explicit non-applicability distinguished as `undocumented` and evidence-backed `not_applicable`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020; Contract §Evidence and surfaces]
- [x] CHK009 Is competing-source authority resolved by narrowest explicit surface, version, and feature applicability rather than recency or local observation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016 and §Clarifications Session 1]
- [x] CHK010 Must every unresolved authority or applicability conflict be classified as `blocking_no_go` or owned `nonblocking_deferred` without supporting an affected conclusion? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019; Data Model §ProvenanceRecord]
- [x] CHK011 Does every relevant evidence, route, candidate, and agent record require a concrete invalidation trigger? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010 and §FR-017; Data Model §AgentRecord and §ProvenanceRecord]
- [x] CHK012 Is the consequence of a fired invalidation trigger explicit both before handoff and after `go`, including failed completion evidence and re-admission? [Recovery Coverage, Spec §FR-017 and §FR-024; Contract §Evidence and surfaces]

## Deterministic Inventory and Artifact Agreement

- [x] CHK013 Is the required agent set exact and immutable at twelve unique names, with ten present routes and absent routes only for `consensus-synthesizer` and `gate-validator`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–FR-003; Contract §Exact agent set and route states]
- [x] CHK014 Are the manifest envelope, agent-centric record shape, required empty arrays, and permitted nulls specified so omissions cannot pass as equivalent values? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications Session 2; Data Model §AgentRecord]
- [x] CHK015 Are contract and route identity rules deterministic for normalization, hashing, stable readable IDs, and ID non-reuse? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008 and §Clarifications Session 2; Data Model §Canonical identity rules]
- [x] CHK016 Is Markdown/JSON agreement required for all twelve names, IDs, hashes, routes or absences, candidate tuples, eligibility, capabilities, rationale, provenance, fixtures, telemetry, unknowns, checks, and terminal state? [Completeness, Spec §FR-024 and §SC-008; Data Model §Cross-artifact agreement projection]
- [x] CHK017 Is lexical stable-ID order explicitly presentation-only so deterministic output cannot imply preference or fallback rank? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications Session 2; Contract §Candidate and policy bounds]
- [x] CHK018 Can the focused checker reproduce the same hashes and handoff state on unchanged artifacts without probing, scoring, qualification, mutation, or a reusable validation framework? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-026–FR-027 and §SC-008–SC-009; Plan §Evidence and Validation Design]

## Fixture, Telemetry, and Unknown Handoff

- [x] CHK019 Is the fixture backlog an exact three-current/nine-missing partition with every named agent assigned one status? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022; Data Model §FixtureContract]
- [x] CHK020 Does every fixture contract specify its path state, representative task and input, expected behavior and output shape, hard-contract assertions, and evidence class? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications Session 3; Contract §Fixture contract]
- [x] CHK021 Are historical prompt-emulation results required to remain `non_release_evidence` rather than silently filling a missing Codex fixture? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022 and §SC-007]
- [x] CHK022 Does every agent have non-empty deferred telemetry requirements that identify the proof, purpose, capability-or-qualification use, and owning downstream spec without claiming unavailable telemetry? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023; Data Model §TelemetryRequirement]
- [x] CHK023 Must every unknown record its class, question, impact, owner, required follow-up, and status, with documentation/inventory closure owned here and capability/qualification deferred only to G56R-002/G56R-003? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023; Data Model §ClassifiedUnknown]
- [x] CHK024 Is an unclassified unknown prohibited from coexisting with `go`, while a fully classified downstream unknown is prevented from becoming an implicit policy conclusion? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §FR-023–FR-025; Contract §Unknowns and handoff]

## One-Working-Day Terminal Decision

- [x] CHK025 Are `started_at`, predeclared `deadline_at`, and `stopped_at` defined as RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offsets and an objectively checkable ordering? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025; Data Model §HandoffDecision]
- [x] CHK026 Does the objective gate enumerate artifact presence, exact 12/10/2 coverage, contracts, candidates, provenance, agreement, fixtures, telemetry, unknowns, sanitization, and conflict disposition? [Completeness, Spec §FR-024; Data Model §HandoffDecision]
- [x] CHK027 Is `go` permitted only when every completion check passes before the deadline with no blocking conflict or unclassified unknown? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-024–FR-025; Contract §Unknowns and handoff]
- [x] CHK028 Does `no_go` identify every unmet gate, requirement reference, available evidence, impact, owner, and follow-up along with completed artifacts and all terminal timestamps? [Completeness, Spec §Clarifications Session 3 and §FR-025; Data Model §HandoffDecision]
- [x] CHK029 Is the deadline terminal without allowing extra time, reduced deliverables, probing, scoring, defect repair, or production mutation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-025 and §FR-027; Contract §Unknowns and handoff]
- [x] CHK030 Can a PR reviewer reproduce the terminal decision and determine whether later evidence or identity drift invalidates G56R-002 admission without undocumented judgment? [Measurability, Spec §FR-024 and §SC-009; Plan §Requirement and Acceptance Traceability]

## Notes

- Initial assessment found two reliability requirement gaps: an objectively recorded workday deadline/offset and explicit pre-/post-handoff consequences for stale, unverifiable, or invalidated evidence. Both were remediated in the feature requirements and contracts before this single re-assessment.
- Check items off as completed: `[x]`.
- This checklist assesses requirements writing for a PR reviewer; it does not test implementation, add platform facts, or authorize candidate execution.
